text:
The Penguins left on their western swing in October with a 10-game stretch that Ryan Wilson of Hockey Hot Stove said could make or break the season. It went 2-7-1. Pittsburgh sits at 5-9-2, tied for the fewest points in the East, and they are winless in four.

Here is the strange part: they have been close to an even team. Pittsburgh has 49% of all expected goals and 52% at five on five, and by the quality of their chances they deserved about 17 points rather than 12. That is a five-point gap, and it is not small. The goaltending owns some of it. Sergei Murashov has a .871 save percentage over his last five starts, 3.9 goals worse than expected, and the team has allowed 2.6 more goals than its chances suggest.

The power play owns the rest. It is producing 0.46 expected goals a game, a thin number for a roster with Sidney Crosby, Evgeni Malkin and Erik Karlsson, which is how you get a headline like "Penguins Power Play Is Dreck." The depth line of Connor Dewar, Blake Lizotte and Nick Robertson has been the most reliable trio, which tells you what the stars are carrying.

Our simulations give them a 19% playoff chance. The process says patience. The standings, and Wilson's line that it may be time for Kyle Dubas to brush up his sales pitches, say there isn't much of it left.
headline: Better than the record, not good enough to wait
